claim_tested: The GLO1 active site is built from both subunits by 3D domain swapping
key_finding: Active site sits in the dimer interface; zinc and inhibitor contact side chains from both subunits; each monomer is two structurally equivalent domains from gene duplication
confidence_and_limitations: High for architecture. Does not address isoform 2.

claim_tested: Identity of the transition-state-analogue complex used for mapping
key_finding: 1QIN is the HIPC-GSH complex; the hydroxycarbamoyl group coordinates zinc directly; a loop closes over the active site on transition-state binding
confidence_and_limitations: High. The closing loop is not localised in the abstract; this analysis localises it to 156-160 and the C-terminus.

claim_tested: Which residues are the catalytic zinc ligands
key_finding: Glu99 and Glu172 are zinc ligands; E172Q has <1e-5 of wild-type activity; Q33E/E172Q is inactive with Zn still bound; Glu172 is the catalytic base
context: Recombinant human GLO1 in E. coli; enzyme kinetics and metal analysis
confidence_and_limitations: High. Establishes that the catalytic residues (UniProt 34/100/127/173) are all outside 105-119.

claim_tested: Do zinc ligands or substrate contacts lie in 105-119
key_finding: Zn shell <2.8 A: Gln33 2.05, Glu99 1.91 (same chain), His126 2.05 (partner chain). No annotated Zn or substrate residue is inside 105-119. Nearest segment atom to Zn is 9.51 A (Asn119)
confidence_and_limitations: High for the measurement. Crystal structure of the canonical protein only.

claim_tested: Does 105-119 form the domain-swapped dimer interface
key_finding: Segment buries 157 A2 of a 3657 A2 chain-A interface = 4.3%; concentrated in His116 56, Trp105 46, Tyr115 24, Asn119 17 A2
context: Crystal structure Shrake-Rupley SASA probe 1.4 A
confidence_and_limitations: High for the measurement. 4.3% is a minority contribution so interface loss alone would not predict inactivity.

claim_tested: Can the isoform 2 polypeptide adopt the canonical fold
key_finding: Ca(104) to Ca(120) is 22.87 A in all chains of three structures; a peptide bond needs ~3.8 A (observed consecutive Ca-Ca mean 3.81 A). 105-119 is the crossover connector from strand 98-104 (Zn ligand Glu100) to strand 128-131 (after Zn ligand His127)
context: Crystal structures of canonical human GLO1
confidence_and_limitations: High as a geometric argument. It is an inference about a protein never expressed or solved; no explicit folding simulation was run.

stance: refutes a variant of the stated mechanism
key_finding: Kabsch over 176 CA, RMSD 0.52 A. Largest shifts at 157 (2.48 A), 183-184 (2.36 A), 182 (2.23 A), 156 (1.96 A). Segment 105-119 mean 0.36 A vs whole-chain mean 0.34 A
confidence_and_limitations: High for the measurement. Two states only.

claim_tested: Can spliceosomal chemistry produce the 45 nt deletion
key_finding: Codons 105-119 = CDS 313-357, entirely inside exon 4 (68 nt CDS). All six windows reproducing the 169-aa protein have flanks CA/GG, AA/GC, AT/CA, TT/AA, TG/AT, GG/TT: no GT..AG, GC..AG or AT..AC. Alternative-acceptor model needs AG at exon-4 nt 44-45, which is GG
confidence_and_limitations: High. Does not exclude exotic recursive or trans-splicing, which have no support here.

claim_tested: How many independent cDNAs support isoform 2
key_finding: 1 of 12 INSDC GLO1 cDNAs (AK293345, FLJ51791) encodes 169 aa; 11 encode 184 aa including NM_006708. A 4 nt direct repeat CAAT flanks the deleted block at mRNA level (chance 3.9e-3)
context: Human cDNA libraries from several projects
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. The repeat is suggestive of RT slippage, not proof. Clone panel is not exhaustive.

key_finding: The single evidence tag on the alternative-sequence feature is ECO:0000303 from a bulk full-length cDNA catalogue; no functional characterisation; no RefSeq, CCDS or Ensembl transcript encodes 169 aa
confidence_and_limitations: High for provenance. ECO:0000303 is an author statement
column9: the weakest evidence class for an isoform.

claim_tested: Is the deleted segment present in the expressed human protein
key_finding: 22 observed peptides cover 137/184 residues; all 15 residues of 105-119 covered twice, including KATLELTHNWGTEDDETQSYHNGNSDPR (96-123). No isoform 2 junction peptide (ATLELTHNSDPR) reported
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Absence of the junction peptide is partly a search-space artefact; most searches use canonical-only or UniProt-with-isoform databases.

claim_tested: Is the 105-119 segment dispensable across evolution
key_finding: Residues 100-125 identical in human, mouse and rat GLO1 (all 184 aa). Metal ligand 2 to ligand 3 spacing is 27 residues in human and mouse, 18 in the 135-aa E. coli Ni-GloA; isoform 2 would give 12
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Only two spacing data points with curated ligand annotation; not a family-wide alignment.
